summary: Raph Levien's original Inconsolata page from the mid-2000s: one unstyled HTML document in browser-default Times, with the name and the character set as PNG images (no webfont at all), a few first-person paragraphs on the design, and links to the source, OTF, PFA and a PDF proof. It is the 'specimen as a plain web page' baseline: the font is shown only as pictures of itself.

instances.look: The only display element: 'Inconsolata' as a black-on-white PNG (~500×63px) in the font itself, top-left, directly followed by body text
instances.learn: Even with no CSS, setting only the title as an image of the font gives the page its identity

reconstruction.layout: h1 containing an 500×63 at the page's default 8px margin, top-left; no hero area, the text starts ~20px below
reconstruction.typography: Name: ~80px Inconsolata Regular rendered into the PNG; everything else is the browser default serif (Times) at 16px

instances.look: Six full-width paragraphs of default Times body text: a dated update note pointing to Google Fonts and GitHub, then the designer's notes on influences and decisions
instances.ux: Inline links to Google Fonts, GitHub, Consolas, TheSansMono and the programmer-fonts list
instances.learn: Name the models and the specific borrowed details (Avenir's 'a', Franklin Gothic's 'g' and 'S', Japanese Gothic micro-serifs): the influences double as a guided look at the glyphs

reconstruction.layout: Unconstrained full-width paragraphs (~1420px measure at 1440 wide), default 16px margins between paragraphs
reconstruction.typography: Browser default serif ~16px, leading ~1.2, black; links default blue underlined
reconstruction.content: 'Inconsolata is my first serious original font release… a monospace font, designed for code listings and the like, in print… First and foremost, Inconsolata is a humanist sans design… also borrows "micro-serifs" from some Japanese Gothic fonts'

instances.look: A PNG of the whole character set as eight monospaced rows in encoding order: ASCII punctuation and digits, A–Z, a–z, Latin-1 symbols, accented capitals and lowercase, Latin Extended, then quotes, arrows and fractions
instances.learn: For a monospace, the glyph set in encoding order as plain rows already forms a perfect grid: no cells needed

reconstruction.layout: Image 609×320 at the left margin, 8 rows of ~33 characters, ~40px row pitch
reconstruction.typography: ~32px Inconsolata Regular, black, characters on the monospace grid
reconstruction.content: Character set from U+0020 upward (ASCII, Latin-1, Latin Extended-A subset, typographic quotes, arrows, fractions)

instances.look: One bracketed link line '[ FontForge source | OpenType file | pfa file | PDF showing ]' under the glyph image, then a paragraph on the Open Font License and TeX Users Group sponsorship with a donation hint
instances.ux: Direct file links (.sfd, .otf, .pfa, PDF test sheet); OFL and TUG Development Fund links
instances.learn: Offering the editable source file next to the binaries signals that the font is truly open

reconstruction.layout: Single text line with pipe separators inside square brackets, then a full-width paragraph
reconstruction.content: File formats offered: FontForge .sfd source, .otf, .pfa, textest.pdf; licence: SIL OFL; sponsor: TUG

instances.look: An h3 'Links' with two bulleted external articles (adding straight quotes, Top 10 Programming Fonts), then two bare footer links 'Other fonts I'm working on.' and 'levien.com'
instances.ux: Text links only; 'Other fonts' leads to the designer's font index
instances.learn: On a one-page specimen, a single 'other fonts' link is the minimum cross-promotion

reconstruction.layout: h3 + ul with default bullets and indent; two links at the bottom-left, no footer bar
reconstruction.typography: h3 default bold ~19px; list and links 16px default serif
reconstruction.content: External articles about the font; link to the designer's other fonts and homepage
